libraries.name: date-fns
libraries.description: Functions for formatting, parsing, and manipulating JavaScript dates.
libraries.goodFor: Picking individual functions for the date operations you need.
libraries.caveat: Date calculations and formatting, rather than a date picker UI.
libraries.implementation: Call the date functions from your application code. Choose formatting patterns and locale behavior explicitly; build or add a separate calendar UI when users need to select a date.

libraries.name: Day.js
libraries.description: A compact date library with a chainable API.
libraries.goodFor: Working with dates through a familiar, chainable API.
libraries.caveat: Add plugins for capabilities beyond the core.
libraries.implementation: Use Day.js objects for parsing, manipulation, and display. Enable the plugins and locales your application needs, and check their behavior against your date formats.

libraries.name: dnd kit
libraries.description: Composable building blocks for dragging, dropping, sorting, and reordering.
libraries.goodFor: Custom sortable lists and drag-and-drop interfaces in React.
libraries.caveat: You still design the interface, interaction rules, and feedback.
libraries.implementation: Connect draggable and droppable elements to your application state. Choose sensors, sorting behavior, and visual feedback; test pointer and keyboard interactions in your actual layout.

libraries.name: Pragmatic drag and drop
libraries.description: Atlassian's drag-and-drop building blocks based on the browser's native capabilities.
libraries.goodFor: Fine-grained control over drop targets and custom interactions.
libraries.caveat: A toolkit to assemble; accessible controls and UI need deliberate design.
libraries.implementation: Wire adapters and drop-target behavior into your existing UI. Add appropriate visual feedback and accessible alternatives for actions that would otherwise require dragging.

libraries.name: TanStack Table
libraries.description: Table logic for sorting, filtering, and pagination, with complete control over your UI.
libraries.goodFor: A custom table that fits your existing design system.
libraries.caveat: You build the markup and controls; virtualization is a separate concern.
libraries.implementation: Render rows and cells using your own components. Connect search, sort, and filter controls to table state. For large datasets, decide between client-side data, server-side operations, and a separate virtualization layer.

libraries.name: AG Grid
libraries.description: A ready-made grid for interactive data-heavy applications.
libraries.goodFor: Rich table interactions with an integrated grid UI.
libraries.caveat: Some advanced features require an Enterprise license.
libraries.implementation: Configure columns, data, and the grid theme, then connect the row model and events to your app. Check the Community and Enterprise feature boundaries for the interactions you need.

libraries.name: MUI X Data Grid
libraries.description: A feature-rich data grid in the MUI component ecosystem.
libraries.goodFor: Data tables in an application already using Material UI.
libraries.caveat: Feature availability differs between Community, Pro, and Premium.
libraries.implementation: Define rows and columns, configure grid features, and apply your MUI theme. Confirm the required plan for advanced interactions before settling on the component.

categories.title: Dates & time
categories.description: Format, parse, and work with dates. Find the right utilities for the way you build.
categories.noteTitle: Working with dates, or choosing a date?
categories.note: These libraries handle date values. A date picker is a separate UI component you can use alongside them.
categories.taskDescription: Format a date, parse a timestamp, or calculate the time between two dates.

categories.title: Drag & drop
categories.description: Reorder a list, move cards between columns, or build your own drag-and-drop interaction.
categories.noteTitle: Start with the interaction you need.
categories.note: Sortable lists and custom drop targets need different building blocks. Plan keyboard interaction and an alternative to dragging from the start.
categories.taskDescription: Drag items to reorder a sortable list, move cards on a kanban board, or drop files into an app.

categories.title: Data tables
categories.description: Search, sort, and filter a large dataset. Choose the right balance of ready-made UI and control.
categories.noteTitle: Table logic, or a complete grid?
categories.note: A headless table gives you the behavior while you build the interface. A data grid provides a UI with a different set of customization and licensing tradeoffs.
categories.taskDescription: I want to display a large dataset in a table with search, sorting, and filtering.
